bill:sjr90:261.title: Modifies provisions relating to the State Tax Commission
bill:sjr90:261.briefDescription: This amendment modifies provisions relating to the State Tax Commission.

bill:sjr91:261.title: Modifies provisions relating to taxation
bill:sjr91:261.briefDescription: This constitutional amendment, if approved by the voters, provides that the rate of income tax imposed by the General Assembly shall not exceed 4.7%.

bill:sjr92:261.title: Increases the debt limit for school districts
bill:sjr92:261.briefDescription: This proposed constitutional amendment, if approved by the voters, increases the debt limit for school districts from 15% to 20% of the value of the district's taxable tangible property.

bill:sjr93:261.title: Allows retrospective laws for certain civil actions relating to sexual abuse of a child
bill:sjr93:261.briefDescription: This constitutional amendment, if approved by the voters, provides that retrospective laws may be enacted for civil claims involving sexual abuse of a child or tortious conduct that caused or contributed to cause sexual abuse to a child.

bill:sjr94:261.briefDescription: This constitutional amendment, if approved by the voters, expands the current exemption from real property taxes for former prisoners of war with a total service-connected disability to all disabled veterans, as defined in the amendment, including surviving spouses of deceased disabled veterans.

bill:sjr98:261.briefDescription: Replaces the property tax on real property with a sales tax

bill:sjr99:261.briefDescription: Modifies provisions of the Constitution relating to powers of the General Assembly

bill:sjr100:261.briefDescription: Prohibits laws or public policies from infringing on the right of individuals to refuse medical procedures or treatments

bill:sjr105:261.title: Provides for the appointment of all appellate judges by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate and for the election of all circuit and associate circuit judges
bill:sjr105:261.briefDescription: Provides for the appointment of all appellate judges by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate and for the election of all circuit and associate circuit judges

bill:sjr106:261.title: Transfers authority over the state highway system to the Department of Transportation
bill:sjr106:261.briefDescription: Current constitutional provisions place the Department of Transportation and the management of the state highway system under the control of the State Highways and Transportation Commission. This constitutional amendment, if approved by the voters, places such control under the Department of Transportation, which shall be lead by a director appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate.

bill:sjr107:261.title: Repeals Article I, Section 36, the "Right to Reproductive Freedom Initiative"
bill:sjr107:261.briefDescription: This constitutional amendment, if adopted by the voters, will repeal Article I, Section 36, the "Right to Reproductive Freedom Initiative".

bill:sjr108:261.title: Modifies provisions relating to work requirements for MO HealthNet
bill:sjr108:261.briefDescription: If approved by the voters, this constitutional amendment requires the Department of Social Services and the MO HealthNet Division to implement work requirements for certain individuals as a condition of participation in the MO HealthNet program. 332.700. 
Sections 332.700 to 332.760 shall be known and cited as the Dentist and 
2Dental Hygienist Compact. The purposes of this Compact are to facilitate the interstate 
3practice of dentistry and dental hygiene and improve public access to dentistry and 
4dental hygiene services by providing Dentists and Dental Hygienists licensed in a 
5Participating State the ability to practice in Participating States in which they are not 
6licensed. The Compact does this by establishing a pathway for Dentists and Dental 
7Hygienists licensed in a Participating State to obtain a Compact Privilege that 
8authorizes them to practice in another Participating State in which they are not licensed. 
9The Compact enables Participating States to protect the public health and safety with 
10respect to the practice of such Dentists and Dental Hygienists, through the State's 
11authority to regulate the practice of dentistry and dental hygiene in the State. The 
12Compact:
HB 
1847 9

13(1) Enables Dentists and Dental Hygienists who qualify for a Compact Privilege 
14to practice in other Participating States without satisfying burdensome and duplicative 
15requirements associated with securing a License to practice in those States;
16(2) 
Promotes mobility and addresses workforce shortages through each 
17Participating State's acceptance of a Compact Privilege to practice in that State;
18(3) 
Increases public access to qualified, licensed Dentists and Dental Hygienists 
19by creating a responsible, streamlined pathway for Licensees to practice in Participating 
20States;
21(4) 
Enhances the ability of Participating States to protect the public's health and 
22safety;
23(5) 
Does not interfere with licensure requirements established by a Participating 
24State;
25(6) 
Facilitates the sharing of licensure and disciplinary information among 
26Participating States;
27(7) 
Requires Dentists and Dental Hygienists who practice in a Participating State 
28pursuant to a Compact Privilege to practice within the Scope of Practice authorized in 
29that State;
30(8) 
Extends the authority of a Participating State to regulate the practice of 
31dentistry and dental hygiene within its borders to Dentists and Dental Hygienists who 
32practice in the State through a Compact Privilege;
33(9) 
Promotes the cooperation of Participating States in regulating the practice of 
34dentistry and dental hygiene within those States;
35(10) 
Facilitates the relocation of military members and their spouses who are 
36licensed to practice dentistry or dental hygiene.

324.1800. 1. Sections 324.1800 to 324.1865 shall be known and may be cited as 
2the "Dietitian Licensure Compact".
32. 
The purpose of this Compact is to facilitate interstate Practice of Dietetics 
4with the goal of improving public access to dietetics services. This Compact preserves 
5the regulatory authority of States to protect public health and safety through the 
6current system of State licensure, while also providing for licensure portability through 
7a Compact Privilege granted to qualifying professionals.
83. 
This Compact is designed to achieve the following objectives:
9(1) 
Increase public access to dietetics services;
10(2) 
Provide opportunities for interstate practice by Licensed Dietitians who meet 
11uniform requirements;
12(3) 
Eliminate the necessity for Licenses in multiple States;
13(4) 
Reduce administrative burden on Member States and Licensees;
14(5) 
Enhance the States' ability to protect the public's health and safety;
15(6) 
Encourage the cooperation of Member States in regulating multistate 
16practice of Licensed Dietitians;
17(7) 
Support relocating Active Military Members and their spouses;
18(8) 
Enhance the exchange of licensure, investigative, and disciplinary 
19information among Member States; and
20(9) 
Vest all Member States with the authority to hold a Licensed Dietitian 
21accountable for meeting all State practice laws in the State in which the patient is 
22located at the time care is rendered.

18and sewer usage charges during the current billing period, meter readings taken at the 
19beginning and end of the current billing period, and the dates those meter readings were 
20taken.
214. 
An owner or operator of premises who seeks to allocate water and sewer usage 
22charges among lessees in accordance with subdivision (2) of subsection 1 of this section 
23and subsection 2 of this section shall first provide to potential lessees a clear and written 
24description of the mathematical formula used to calculate and allocate water and sewer 
25usage charges prior to the commencement of a lease.
265. 
The total amount of water and sewer usage charges billed to lessees in 
27accordance with subsections 1 and 2 of this section shall not exceed the amount charged 
28to the owner or operator by the public utility or state-certified corporation, including 
29applicable taxes and surcharges.
306. 
An owner or operator may charge and collect from lessees reasonable fees for 
31costs incurred by the owner or operator related to the provision of administrative 
32services undertaken to implement water and sewer usage billing in accordance with 
33subsections 1 and 2 of this section, provided that such charges are first disclosed to 
34lessees prior to the commencement of a lease.
357. 
An owner or operator may charge and collect from lessees a fee for late 
36payment of charges billed to lessees in accordance with subsections 1 and 2 of this 
37section. The late charge shall be deemed as rent.
388. 
An owner or operator of premises may hire a third-party provider to carry 
39out water and sewer usage billing services in accordance with subsections 1 and 2 of this 
40section. In carrying out water and sewer usage billing services on behalf of an owner or 
41operator of a premises, a third-party water and sewer usage billing provider shall 
42comply with subsections 3, 4, and 5 of this section.
439. 
An owner's or operator's third-party water and sewer usage billing provider 
44may charge and collect from lessees reasonable fees for costs incurred related to the 
45provision of administrative services undertaken to implement water and sewer usage 
46billing in accordance with subsection 6 of this section.
4710. 
An owner's or operator's third-party water and sewer usage billing provider 
48may charge and collect from lessees a fee for late payment of charges billed to lessees in 
49accordance with subsection 7 of this section. The late charge shall be deemed as rent.

SECOND REGULAR SESSION 
SENATE BILL NO. 988 
103RD GENERAL ASSEMBLY 
 
INTRODUCED BY SENATOR BROWN (26). 
4727S.01I KRISTINA MARTIN, Secretary 
 
AN ACT 
To amend chapter 332, RSMo, by adding thereto one new section relating to licensure of dentists 
and dental hygienists. 
 
Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Missouri, as follows: 
     Section A.  Chapter 332, RSMo, is amended by adding thereto 1 
one new section, to be known as section 332.700, to read as 2 
follows:3 
     332.700.  SECTION 1.  TITLE AND PURPOSE 1 
     This statute shall be known and cited as the Dentist  2 
and Dental Hygienist Compact.  The purposes of this Compact  3 
are to facilitate the interstate practice of dentistry and  4 
dental hygiene and improve public access to dentistry and  5 
dental hygiene services by providing Dentists and Dental  6 
Hygienists licensed in a Participating State the ability to  7 
practice in Participating States in which they are not  8 
licensed.  The Compact does this by establishing a pathway  9 
for Dentists and Dental Hygienists licensed in a  10 
Participating State to obtain a Compact Privilege that  11 
authorizes them to practice in another Participating State  12 
in which they are not licensed.  The Compact enables  13 
Participating States to protect the public health and safety  14 
with respect to the practice of such Dentists and Dental  15 
Hygienists, through the State's authority to regulate the  16 

 SB 988 2 
practice of dentistry and dental hygiene in the State.  The  17 
Compact: 18 
     A.  Enables Dentists and Dental Hygienists who qualify  19 
for a Compact Privilege to practice in other Participating  20 
States without satisfying burdensome and duplicative  21 
requirements associated with securing a License to practice  22 
in those States; 23 
     B.  Promotes mobility and addresses workforce shortages  24 
through each Participating State's acceptance of a Compact  25 
Privilege to practice in that State; 26 
     C.  Increases public access to qualified, licensed  27 
Dentists and Dental Hygienists by creating a responsible,  28 
streamlined pathway for Licensees to practice in  29 
Participating States; 30 
     D.  Enhances the ability of Participating States to  31 
protect the public's health and safety; 32 
     E.  Does not interfere with licensure requirements  33 
established by a Participating State; 34 
     F.  Facilitates the sharing of licensure and  35 
disciplinary information among Participating States; 36 
     G.  Requires Dentists and Dental Hygienists who  37 
practice in a Participating State pursuant to a Compact  38 
Privilege to practice within the Scope of Practice  39 
authorized in that State; 40 
     H.  Extends the authority of a Participating State to  41 
regulate the practice of dentistry and dental hygiene within  42 
its borders to Dentists and Dental Hygienists who practice  43 
in the State through a Compact Privilege; 44 
     I.  Promotes the cooperation of Participating States in  45 
regulating the practice of dentistry and dental hygiene  46 
within those States; 47 

 SB 988 3 
     J.  Facilitates the relocation of military members and  48 
their spouses who are licensed to practice dentistry or  49 
dental hygiene; 50 
     SECTION 2.  DEFINITIONS 51 
     As used in this Compact, unless the context requires  52 
otherwise, the following definitions shall apply: 53 
     A. "Active Military Member" means any person with full- 54 
time duty status in the armed forces of the United States,  55 
including members of the National Guard and Reserve. 56 
     B.  "Adverse Action" means disciplinary action or  57 
encumbrance imposed on a License or Compact Privilege by a  58 
State Licensing Authority. 59 
     C.  "Alternative Program" means a non-disciplinary  60 
monitoring or practice remediation process applicable to a  61 
Dentist or Dental Hygienist approved by a State Licensing  62 
Authority of a Participating State in which the Dentist or  63 
Dental Hygienist is licensed.  This includes, but is not  64 
limited to, programs to which Licensees with substance abuse  65 
or addiction issues are referred in lieu of Adverse Action. 66 
     D.  "Clinical Assessment" means examination or process,  67 
required for licensure as a Dentist or Dental Hygienist as  68 
applicable, that provides evidence of clinical competence in  69 
dentistry or dental hygiene. 70 
     E.  "Commissioner" means the individual appointed by a  71 
Participating State to serve as the member of the Commission  72 
for that Participating State. 73 
     F.  "Compact" means this Dentist and Dental Hygienist  74 
Compact. 75 
     G.  "Compact Privilege" means the authorization granted  76 
by a Remote State to allow a Licensee from a Participating  77 
State to practice as a Dentist or Dental Hygienist in a  78 
Remote State. 79 

 SB 988 4 
     H.  "Continuing Professional Development" means a  80 
requirement, as a condition of License renewal to provide  81 
evidence of successful participation in educational or  82 
professional activities relevant to practice or area of work. 83 
     I.  "Criminal Background Check" means the submission of  84 
fingerprints or other biometric-based information for a  85 
License applicant for the purpose of obtaining that  86 
applicant's criminal history record information, as defined  87 
in 28 C.F.R. § 20.3(d) from the Federal Bureau of  88 
Investigation and the State's criminal history record  89 
repository as defined in 28 C.F.R. § 20.3(f). 90 
     J.  "Data System" means the Commission's repository of  91 
information about Licensees, including but not limited to  92 
examination, licensure, investigative, Compact Privilege,  93 
Adverse Action, and Alternative Program. 94 
     K.  "Dental Hygienist" means an individual who is  95 
licensed by a State Licensing Authority to practice dental  96 
hygiene. 97 
     L.  "Dentist" means an individual who is licensed by a  98 
State Licensing Authority to practice dentistry. 99 
     M.  "Dentist and Dental Hygienist Compact Commission"  100 
or "Commission" means a joint government agency established  101 
by this Compact comprised of each State that has enacted the  102 
Compact and a national administrative body comprised of a  103 
Commissioner from each State that has enacted the Compact. 104 
     N.  "Encumbered License" means a License that a State  105 
Licensing Authority has limited in any way other than  106 
through an Alternative Program. 107 
     O.  "Executive Board" means the Chair, Vice Chair,  108 
Secretary and Treasurer and any other Commissioners as may  109 
be determined by Commission Rule or bylaw. 110 

 SB 988 5 
     P.  "Jurisprudence Requirement" means the assessment of  111 
an individual's knowledge of the laws and Rules governing  112 
the practice of dentistry or dental hygiene, as applicable,  113 
in a State. 114 
     Q.  "License" means current authorization by a State,  115 
other than authorization pursuant to a Compact Privilege, or  116 
other privilege, for an individual to practice as a Dentist  117 
or Dental Hygienist in that State. 118 
     R.  "Licensee" means an individual who holds an  119 
unrestricted License from a Participating State to practice  120 
as a Dentist or Dental Hygienist in that State. 121 
     S.  "Model Compact" the model for the Dentist and  122 
Dental Hygienist Compact on file with the Council of State  123 
Governments or other entity as designated by the Commission. 124 
     T.  "Participating State" means a State that has  125 
enacted the Compact and been admitted to the Commission in  126 
accordance with the provisions herein and Commission Rules. 127 
     U.  "Qualifying License" means a License that is not an  128 
Encumbered License issued by a Participating State to  129 
practice dentistry or dental hygiene. 130 
     V.  "Remote State" means a Participating State where a  131 
Licensee who is not licensed as a Dentist or Dental  132 
Hygienist is exercising or seeking to exercise the Compact  133 
Privilege. 134 
     W.  "Rule" means a regulation promulgated by an entity  135 
that has the force of law. 136 
     X.  "Scope of Practice" means the procedures, actions,  137 
and processes a Dentist or Dental Hygienist licensed in a  138 
State is permitted to undertake in that State and the  139 
circumstances under which the Licensee is permitted to  140 
undertake those procedures, actions and processes.  Such  141 
procedures, actions and processes and the circumstances  142 

 SB 988 6 
under which they may be undertaken may be established  143 
through means, including, but not limited to, statute,  144 
regulations, case law, and other processes available to the  145 
State Licensing Authority or other government agency. 146 
     Y.  "Significant Investigative Information" means  147 
information, records, and documents received or generated by  148 
a State Licensing Authority pursuant to an investigation for  149 
which a determination has been made that there is probable  150 
cause to believe that the Licensee has violated a statute or  151 
regulation that is considered more than a minor infraction  152 
for which the State Licensing Authority could pursue Adverse  153 
Action against the Licensee. 154 
     Z.  "State" means any state, commonwealth, district, or  155 
territory of the United States of America that regulates the  156 
practices of dentistry and dental hygiene. 157 
     AA.  "State Licensing Authority" means an agency or  158 
other entity of a State that is responsible for the  159 
licensing and regulation of Dentists or Dental Hygienists. 160 
     SECTION 3.  STATE PARTICIPATION IN THE COMPACT 161 
     A.  In order to join the Compact and thereafter  162 
continue as a Participating State, a State must: 163 
     1.  Enact a compact that is not materially different  164 
from the Model Compact as determined in accordance with  165 
Commission Rules; 166 
     2.  Participate fully in the Commission's Data System; 167 
     3.  Have a mechanism in place for receiving and  168 
investigating complaints about its Licensees and License  169 
applicants; 170 
     4.  Notify the Commission, in compliance with the terms  171 
of the Compact and Commission Rules, of any Adverse Action  172 
or the availability of Significant Investigative Information  173 
regarding a Licensee and License applicant; 174 

 SB 988 7 
     5.  Fully implement a Criminal Background Check  175 
requirement, within a time frame established by Commission  176 
Rule, by receiving the results of a qualifying Criminal  177 
Background Check; 178 
     6.  Comply with the Commission Rules applicable to a  179 
Participating State; 180 
     7.  Accept the National Board Examinations of the Joint  181 
Commission on National Dental Examinations or another  182 
examination accepted by Commission Rule as a licensure  183 
examination; 184 
     8.  Accept for licensure that applicants for a Dentist  185 
License graduate from a predoctoral dental education program  186 
accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation, or  187 
another accrediting agency recognized by the United States  188 
Department of Education for the accreditation of dentistry  189 
and dental hygiene education programs, leading to the Doctor  190 
of Dental Surgery (D.D.S.) or Doctor of Dental Medicine  191 
(D.M.D.) degree; 192 
     9.  Accept for licensure that applicants for a Dental  193 
Hygienist License graduate from a dental hygiene education  194 
program accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation  195 
or another accrediting agency recognized by the United  196 
States Department of Education for the accreditation of  197 
dentistry and dental hygiene education programs; 198 
     10.  Require for licensure that applicants successfully  199 
complete a Clinical Assessment; 200 
     11.  Have Continuing Professional Development  201 
requirements as a condition for License renewal; and 202 
     12.  Pay a participation fee to the Commission as  203 
established by Commission Rule. 204 

 SB 988 8 
     B.  Providing alternative pathways for an individual to  205 
obtain an unrestricted License does not disqualify a State  206 
from participating in the Compact. 207 
     C.  When conducting a Criminal Background Check the  208 
State Licensing Authority shall: 209 
     1.  Consider that information in making a licensure  210 
decision; 211 
     2.  Maintain documentation of completion of the  212 
Criminal Background Check and background check information  213 
to the extent allowed by State and federal law; and 214 
     3.  Report to the Commission whether it has completed  215 
the Criminal Background Check and whether the individual was  216 
granted or denied a License. 217 
     D.  A Licensee of a Participating State who has a  218 
Qualifying License in that State and does not hold an  219 
Encumbered License in any other Participating State, shall  220 
be issued a Compact Privilege in a Remote State in  221 
accordance with the terms of the Compact and Commission  222 
Rules.  If a Remote State has a Jurisprudence Requirement a  223 
Compact Privilege will not be issued to the Licensee unless  224 
the Licensee has satisfied the Jurisprudence Requirement. 225 
     SECTION 4.  COMPACT PRIVILEGE 226 
     A.  To obtain and exercise the Compact Privilege under  227 
the terms and provisions of the Compact, the Licensee shall: 228 
     1.  Have a Qualifying License as a Dentist or Dental  229 
Hygienist in a Participating State; 230 
     2.  Be eligible for a Compact Privilege in any Remote  231 
State in accordance with D, G and H of this section; 232 
     3.  Submit to an application process whenever the  233 
Licensee is seeking a Compact Privilege; 234 
     4.  Pay any applicable Commission and Remote State fees  235 
for a Compact Privilege in the Remote State; 236 

 SB 988 9 
     5.  Meet any Jurisprudence Requirement established by a  237 
Remote State in which the Licensee is seeking a Compact  238 
Privilege; 239 
     6.  Have passed a National Board Examination of the  240 
Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations or another  241 
examination accepted by Commission Rule; 242 
     7.  For a Dentist, have graduated from a predoctoral  243 
dental education program accredited by the Commission on  244 
Dental Accreditation, or another accrediting agency  245 
recognized by the United States Department of Education for  246 
the accreditation of dentistry and dental hygiene education  247 
programs, leading to the Doctor of Dental Surgery (D.D.S.)  248 
or Doctor of Dental Medicine (D.M.D.) degree; 249 
     8.  For a Dental Hygienist, have graduated from a  250 
dental hygiene education program accredited by the  251 
Commission on Dental Accreditation or another accrediting  252 
agency recognized by the United States Department of  253 
Education for the accreditation of dentistry and dental  254 
hygiene education programs; 255 
     9.  Have successfully completed a Clinical Assessment  256 
for licensure; 257 
     10.  Report to the Commission Adverse Action taken by  258 
any non-Participating State when applying for a Compact  259 
Privilege and, otherwise, within thirty (30) days from the  260 
date the Adverse Action is taken; 261 
     11.  Report to the Commission when applying for a  262 
Compact Privilege the address of the Licensee's primary  263 
residence and thereafter immediately report to the  264 
Commission any change in the address of the Licensee's  265 
primary residence; and 266 
     12.  Consent to accept service of process by mail at  267 
the Licensee's primary residence on record with the  268 

 SB 988 10 
Commission with respect to any action brought against the  269 
Licensee by the Commission or a Participating State, and  270 
consent to accept service of a subpoena by mail at the  271 
Licensee's primary residence on record with the Commission  272 
with respect to any action brought or investigation  273 
conducted by the Commission or a Participating State. 274 
     B.  The Licensee must comply with the requirements of  275 
subsection A of this section to maintain the Compact  276 
Privilege in the Remote State.  If those requirements are  277 
met, the Compact Privilege will continue as long as the  278 
Licensee maintains a Qualifying License in the State through  279 
which the Licensee applied for the Compact Privilege and  280 
pays any applicable Compact Privilege renewal fees. 281 
     C.  A Licensee providing dentistry or dental hygiene in  282 
a Remote State under the Compact Privilege shall function  283 
within the Scope of Practice authorized by the Remote State  284 
for a Dentist or Dental Hygienist licensed in that State. 285 
     D.  A Licensee providing dentistry or dental hygiene  286 
pursuant to a Compact Privilege in a Remote State is subject  287 
to that State's regulatory authority.  A Remote State may,  288 
in accordance with due process and that State's laws, by  289 
Adverse Action revoke or remove a Licensee's Compact  290 
Privilege in the Remote State for a specific period of time  291 
and impose fines or take any other necessary actions to  292 
protect the health and safety of its citizens.  If a Remote  293 
State imposes an Adverse Action against a Compact Privilege  294 
that limits the Compact Privilege, that Adverse Action  295 
applies to all Compact Privileges in all Remote States.  A  296 
Licensee whose Compact Privilege in a Remote State is  297 
removed for a specified period of time is not eligible for a  298 
Compact Privilege in any other Remote State until the  299 

 SB 988 11 
specific time for removal of the Compact Privilege has  300 
passed and all encumbrance requirements are satisfied. 301 
     E.  If a License in a Participating State is an  302 
Encumbered License, the Licensee shall lose the Compact  303 
Privilege in a Remote State and shall not be eligible for a  304 
Compact Privilege in any Remote State until the License is  305 
no longer encumbered. 306 
     F.  Once an Encumbered License in a Participating State  307 
is restored to good standing, the Licensee must meet the  308 
requirements of subsection A of this section to obtain a  309 
Compact Privilege in a Remote State. 310 
     G.  If a Licensee's Compact Privilege in a Remote State  311 
is removed by the Remote State, the individual shall lose or  312 
be ineligible for the Compact Privilege in any Remote State  313 
until the following occur: 314 
     1.  The specific period of time for which the Compact  315 
Privilege was removed has ended; and 316 
     2.  All conditions for removal of the Compact Privilege  317 
have been satisfied. 318 
     H.  Once the requirements of subsection G of this  319 
section have been met, the Licensee must meet the  320 
requirements in subsection A of this section to obtain a  321 
Compact Privilege in a Remote State. 322 
     SECTION 5.  ACTIVE MILITARY MEMBER OR THEIR SPOUSES 323 
     An Active Military Member and their spouse shall not be  324 
required to pay to the Commission for a Compact Privilege  325 
the fee otherwise charged by the Commission.  If a Remote  326 
State chooses to charge a fee for a Compact Privilege, it  327 
may choose to charge a reduced fee or no fee to an Active  328 
Military Member and their spouse for a Compact Privilege. 329 
     SECTION 6.  ADVERSE ACTIONS 330 

 SB 988 12 
     A.  A Participating State in which a Licensee is  331 
licensed shall have exclusive authority to impose Adverse  332 
Action against the Qualifying License issued by that  333 
Participating State. 334 
     B.  A Participating State may take Adverse Action based  335 
on the Significant Investigative Information of a Remote  336 
State, so long as the Participating State follows its own  337 
procedures for imposing Adverse Action. 338 
     C.  Nothing in this Compact shall override a  339 
Participating State's decision that participation in an  340 
Alternative Program may be used in lieu of Adverse Action  341 
and that such participation shall remain non-public if  342 
required by the Participating State's laws.  Participating  343 
States must require Licensees who enter any Alternative  344 
Program in lieu of discipline to agree not to practice  345 
pursuant to a Compact Privilege in any other Participating  346 
State during the term of the Alternative Program without  347 
prior authorization from such other Participating State. 348 
     D.  Any Participating State in which a Licensee is  349 
applying to practice or is practicing pursuant to a Compact  350 
Privilege may investigate actual or alleged violations of  351 
the statutes and regulations authorizing the practice of  352 
dentistry or dental hygiene in any other Participating State  353 
in which the Dentist or Dental Hygienist holds a License or  354 
Compact Privilege. 355 
     E.  A Remote State shall have the authority to: 356 
     1.  Take Adverse Actions as set forth in Section 4.D  357 
against a Licensee's Compact Privilege in the State; 358 
     2.  In furtherance of its rights and responsibilities  359 
under the Compact and the Commission's Rules issue subpoenas  360 
for both hearings and investigations that require the  361 
attendance and testimony of witnesses, and the production of  362 

 SB 988 13 
evidence.  Subpoenas issued by a State Licensing Authority  363 
in a Participating State for the attendance and testimony of  364 
witnesses, or the production of evidence from another  365 
Participating State, shall be enforced in the latter State  366 
by any court of competent jurisdiction, according to the  367 
practice and procedure of that court applicable to subpoenas  368 
issued in proceedings pending before it.  The issuing  369 
authority shall pay any witness fees, travel expenses,  370 
mileage, and other fees required by the service statutes of  371 
the State where the witnesses or evidence are located; and 372 
     3.  If otherwise permitted by State law, recover from  373 
the Licensee the costs of investigations and disposition of  374 
cases resulting from any Adverse Action taken against that  375 
Licensee. 376 
     F.  Joint Investigations 377 
     1.  In addition to the authority granted to a  378 
Participating State by its Dentist or Dental Hygienist  379 
licensure act or other applicable State law, a Participating  380 
State may jointly investigate Licensees with other  381 
Participating States. 382 
     2.  Participating States shall share any Significant  383 
Investigative Information, litigation, or compliance  384 
materials in furtherance of any joint or individual  385 
investigation initiated under the Compact. 386 
     G.  Authority to Continue Investigation 387 
     1.  After a Licensee's Compact Privilege in a Remote  388 
State is terminated, the Remote State may continue an  389 
investigation of the Licensee that began when the Licensee  390 
had a Compact Privilege in that Remote State. 391 
     2.  If the investigation yields what would be  392 
Significant Investigative Information had the Licensee  393 
continued to have a Compact Privilege in that Remote State,  394 

 SB 988 14 
the Remote State shall report the presence of such  395 
information to the Data System as required by Section 8.B.6  396 
as if it was Significant Investigative Information. 397 
     SECTION 7.  ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF THE  398 
COMMISSION 399 
     A.  The Compact Participating States hereby create and  400 
establish a joint government agency whose membership  401 
consists of all Participating States that have enacted the  402 
Compact.  The Commission is an instrumentality of the  403 
Participating States acting jointly and not an  404 
instrumentality of any one State.  The Commission shall come  405 
into existence on or after the effective date of the Compact  406 
as set forth in Section 11A. 407 
     B.  Participation, Voting, and Meetings 408 
     1.  Each Participating State shall have and be limited  409 
to one (1) Commissioner selected by that Participating  410 
State's State Licensing Authority or, if the State has more  411 
than one State Licensing Authority, selected collectively by  412 
the State Licensing Authorities. 413 
     2.  The Commissioner shall be a member or designee of  414 
such Authority or Authorities. 415 
     3.  The Commission may by Rule or bylaw establish a  416 
term of office for Commissioners and may by Rule or bylaw  417 
establish term limits. 418 
     4.  The Commission may recommend to a State Licensing  419 
Authority or Authorities, as applicable, removal or  420 
suspension of an individual as the State's Commissioner. 421 
     5.  A Participating State's State Licensing Authority,  422 
or Authorities, as applicable, shall fill any vacancy of its  423 
Commissioner on the Commission within sixty (60) days of the  424 
vacancy. 425 

 SB 988 15 
     6.  Each Commissioner shall be entitled to one vote on  426 
all matters that are voted upon by the Commission. 427 
     7.  The Commission shall meet at least once during each  428 
calendar year.  Additional meetings may be held as set forth  429 
in the bylaws.  The Commission may meet by  430 
telecommunication, video conference or other similar  431 
electronic means. 432 
     C.  The Commission shall have the following powers: 433 
     1.  Establish the fiscal year of the Commission; 434 
     2.  Establish a code of conduct and conflict of  435 
interest policies; 436 
     3.  Adopt Rules and bylaws; 437 
     4.  Maintain its financial records in accordance with  438 
the bylaws; 439 
     5.  Meet and take such actions as are consistent with  440 
the provisions of this Compact, the Commission's Rules, and  441 
the bylaws; 442 
     6.  Initiate and conclude legal proceedings or actions  443 
in the name of the Commission, provided that the standing of  444 
any State Licensing Authority to sue or be sued under  445 
applicable law shall not be affected; 446 
     7.  Maintain and certify records and information  447 
provided to a Participating State as the authenticated  448 
business records of the Commission, and designate a person  449 
to do so on the Commission's behalf; 450 
     8.  Purchase and maintain insurance and bonds; 451 
     9.  Borrow, accept, or contract for services of  452 
personnel, including, but not limited to, employees of a  453 
Participating State; 454 
     10.  Conduct an annual financial review; 455 
     11.  Hire employees, elect or appoint officers, fix  456 
compensation, define duties, grant such individuals  457 

 SB 988 16 
appropriate authority to carry out the purposes of the  458 
Compact, and establish the Commission's personnel policies  459 
and programs relating to conflicts of interest,  460 
qualifications of personnel, and other related personnel  461 
matters; 462 
     12.  As set forth in the Commission Rules, charge a fee  463 
to a Licensee for the grant of a Compact Privilege in a  464 
Remote State and thereafter, as may be established by  465 
Commission Rule, charge the Licensee a Compact Privilege  466 
renewal fee for each renewal period in which that Licensee  467 
exercises or intends to exercise the Compact Privilege in  468 
that Remote State.  Nothing herein shall be construed to  469 
prevent a Remote State from charging a Licensee a fee for a  470 
Compact Privilege or renewals of a Compact Privilege, or a  471 
fee for the Jurisprudence Requirement if the Remote State  472 
imposes such a requirement for the grant of a Compact  473 
Privilege; 474 
     13.  Accept any and all appropriate gifts, donations,  475 
grants of money, other sources of revenue, equipment,  476 
supplies, materials, and services, and receive, utilize, and  477 
dispose of the same; provided that at all times the  478 
Commission shall avoid any appearance of impropriety and/or  479 
conflict of interest; 480 
     14.  Lease, purchase, retain, own, hold, improve, or  481 
use any property, real, personal, or mixed, or any undivided  482 
interest therein; 483 
     15.  Sell, convey, mortgage, pledge, lease, exchange,  484 
abandon, or otherwise dispose of any property real,  485 
personal, or mixed; 486 
     16.  Establish a budget and make expenditures; 487 
     17.  Borrow money; 488 

 SB 988 17 
     18.  Appoint committees, including standing committees,  489 
which may be composed of members, State regulators, State  490 
legislators or their representatives, and consumer  491 
representatives, and such other interested persons as may be  492 
designated in this Compact and the bylaws; 493 
     19.  Provide and receive information from, and  494 
cooperate with, law enforcement agencies; 495 
     20.  Elect a Chair, Vice Chair, Secretary and Treasurer  496 
and such other officers of the Commission as provided in the  497 
Commission's bylaws; 498

summary:sb834:261:ai.plainLanguage: This bill sets rules for when banks modify home loans. If your mortgage terms change (like interest rate or payment amount), the bank keeps its legal claim on your house. The bank doesn't have to file new paperwork at the courthouse for every change. This protects both homeowners and banks during loan modifications.
summary:sb834:261:ai.technicalSummary: Establishes the Uniform Mortgage Modification Act. Modified mortgages continue securing underlying obligations. Modifications do not affect mortgage priority or lien position regardless of public recording. Modifications excluded from novation classification. Supersedes federal E-SIGN Act provisions with limited exceptions.
keyProvisions: Lien position preserved regardless of modification terms
